findings.title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count, so this definition replaces the width/height version immediately above it. Existing calls to downsize(from, to, width, height, opts) now raise ArgumentError, while calls without an options hash bind height to opts and fail at opts[:allow_animation]. Preserve the existing width/height interface by handling both argument forms in one method or giving percentage downsizing a separate name.

findings.title: The new reduction path cannot preserve animated GIF uploads
findings.body: Animated-image dispatch checks whether tempfile.path ends in .gif, not the uploaded filename or actual format. An extensionless multipart tempfile therefore uses convert's [0] branch and overwrites the original with only its first frame, even when animation is enabled. If the tempfile does have a .gif suffix, the animated branch passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which expects pixel dimensions rather than a percentage and fails. Oversized animated GIFs are consequently either silently flattened or left oversized and rejected. Detect animation independently of the temporary filename and use GIF-compatible resizing instructions.

findings.title: Keep the configured size limit for attachments
findings.body: The fixed 10 MB limit applies to attachments as well as images, although the server only downsizes images. This stops honoring max_attachment_size_kb: a 12 MB attachment allowed by a configured 20 MB limit is now rejected by the browser, while an attachment exceeding a smaller configured limit is uploaded before the server rejects it. Relax validation only for images and retain the configured attachment limit.
